text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access an API, you usually need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. You should also be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because requests can fail for many reasons, and your program should respond gracefully.
